regimens.indication: Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (AChR-Ab Positive) — Adults (>= 40 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive.

The recommended intravenous (IV) ULTOMIRIS loading and maintenance dosing in adult and pediatric patients, one month of age or older weighing 5 kg or greater, with PNH or aHUS, or in adult patients with gMG, NMOSD or IgAN weighing 40 kg or greater, is based on the patient's body weight, as shown in Table 1

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion through a 0.2 or 0.22 micron filter (dilute to 50 mg/mL): 40 to <60 kg: 2,400 mg load then 3,000 mg q8w; 60 to <100 kg: 2,700 mg load then 3,300 mg q8w; >=100 kg: 3,000 mg load then 3,600 mg q8w. First maintenance dose 2 weeks after loading dose. Vaccinate against meningococcal serogroups A, C, W, Y, B >=2 weeks prior.

regimens.indication: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (AQP4-Ab Positive) — Adults (>= 40 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody-positive.
Vaccinate patients against meningococcal infection (serogroups A, C, W, Y and B) according to current ACIP recommendations at least 2 weeks prior to initiation of ULTOMIRIS

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion through a 0.2 or 0.22 micron filter: 40 to <60 kg: 2,400 mg load then 3,000 mg q8w; 60 to <100 kg: 2,700 mg load then 3,300 mg q8w; >=100 kg: 3,000 mg load then 3,600 mg q8w. First maintenance dose 2 weeks after loading dose.

regimens.indication: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) — Adults and Pediatrics (>= 1 month, >= 20 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients one month of age and older with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion: 20 to <30 kg: 900 mg load then 2,100 mg q8w; 30 to <40 kg: 1,200 mg load then 2,700 mg q8w; 40 to <60 kg: 2,400 mg load then 3,000 mg q8w; 60 to <100 kg: 2,700 mg load then 3,300 mg q8w; >=100 kg: 3,000 mg load then 3,600 mg q8w. Maintenance starts 2 weeks after loading dose.

regimens.indication: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) — Pediatrics (>= 1 month, 5 to < 20 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients one month of age and older with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).
The safety and effectiveness of ULTOMIRIS for the treatment of PNH have been established in pediatric patients aged one month and older.

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion: 5 to <10 kg: 600 mg load then 300 mg every 4 weeks; 10 to <20 kg: 600 mg load then 600 mg every 4 weeks. Maintenance starts 2 weeks after loading dose.

regimens.indication: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS) — Adults and Pediatrics (>= 1 month, >= 20 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients one month of age and older with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) to inhibit complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion: 20 to <30 kg: 900 mg load then 2,100 mg q8w; 30 to <40 kg: 1,200 mg load then 2,700 mg q8w; 40 to <60 kg: 2,400 mg load then 3,000 mg q8w; 60 to <100 kg: 2,700 mg load then 3,300 mg q8w; >=100 kg: 3,000 mg load then 3,600 mg q8w. Not indicated for STEC-HUS.

regimens.indication: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS) — Pediatrics (>= 1 month, 5 to < 20 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients one month of age and older with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) to inhibit complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion: 5 to <10 kg: 600 mg load then 300 mg every 4 weeks; 10 to <20 kg: 600 mg load then 600 mg every 4 weeks. Maintenance starts 2 weeks after loading dose. Not indicated for STEC-HUS.

regimens.indication: Primary Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy (IgAN) — Adults (>= 40 kg)

refs.quote: ULTOMIRIS is indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) at risk for disease progression.

regimens.dose_text: Weight-tiered IV infusion: 40 to <60 kg: 2,400 mg load then 3,000 mg q8w; 60 to <100 kg: 2,700 mg load then 3,300 mg q8w; >=100 kg: 3,000 mg load then 3,600 mg q8w. Maintenance starts 2 weeks after loading dose.

regimens.indication: Supplemental Dosing Following Plasma Exchange (PE), Plasmapheresis (PP), or IVIg — Adults (>= 40 kg)

refs.quote: Plasma exchange (PE), plasmapheresis (PP), and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) have been shown to reduce ULTOMIRIS serum levels. A supplemental dose of ULTOMIRIS is required in the setting of PE, PP, or IVIg (Table 3).

regimens.dose_text: Administer within 4 hours after each PE/PP intervention or completion of IVIg cycle. For PE/PP: 40 to <60 kg: 1,200 mg (if recent 2,400 mg) or 1,500 mg (if recent 3,000 mg); 60 to <100 kg: 1,500 mg (if recent 2,700 mg) or 1,800 mg (if recent 3,300 mg); >=100 kg: 1,500 mg (if recent 3,000 mg) or 1,800 mg (if recent 3,600 mg). For IVIg: 600 mg across all >=40 kg tiers.

value.drug_or_class: Plasma Exchange, Plasmapheresis, or Intravenous Immunoglobulins (IVIg)
value.effect: Plasmapheresis or high-dose IVIg clears ravulizumab prematurely, significantly lowering therapeutic complement C5-inhibitory levels.
value.management: Concomitant use requires a supplemental dose of ravulizumab according to official prescribing weight-tiered tables.

refs.quote: Plasma Exchange, Plasmapheresis, or Intravenous Immunoglobulins: concomitant use requires supplemental dose of ULTOMIRIS.

value.drug_or_class: Neonatal Fc Receptor Blockers (FcRn Inhibitors, e.g., Efgartigimod)
value.effect: FcRn blockers promote lysosomal degradation of ravulizumab, lowering its systemic exposure and accelerating clearance.
value.management: Closely monitor for reduced complement inhibition and therapeutic failure of ravulizumab if coadministered with FcRn blockers.
